newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Feb 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The government estimated economic growth in 1997/98 would be 5.5 percent due to expected improvements in domestic demand and foreign trade.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Next Group, headed by businessman Jimmy Lai, known for his criticism of China, will explain on Friday why its plan to seek a listing on the Hong Kong stock exchange had been hindered. The original guarantor changed its mind. Many securities companies and commercial banks did not want to help Next for fear of offending China.

-- MING PAO -- Hongkong Bank and Hang Seng Bank announced lower interest rates for mortgages in an effort to gain more business. With the two biggest banks joining the battle, it was expected that competition in the mortgage market would heat up.

-- Chinese actress Gong Li called on the authorities to loosen their control over films and other artistic activities, saying wrong policies were most responsible for the sluggish film industry in China.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- The chairman of the 8th Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference meeting in Beijing called on representatives to unite around the new leadership with President Jiang Zemin at its core.

-- Chinese Premier Li Peng would stress in his government work report to be delivered at the conference of the National People's Congress on Saturday that Hong Kong was heading towards an optimistic future and that the central government would stick to the "one country, two systems" principle.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Governor Chris Patten was noncommittal in the face of pleas for Britain to go to the United Nations over the provisional legislature and the scrapping of laws on civil liberties.
-- Economists said the government's economic forecasts for the year were broadly in line with the market consensus, and some predicted the figures could end up being conservative.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- The police had decided to protect members of the Provisional Legislative Council against protesters despite the government's pledge not to provide assistance to the interim body.
-- Hong Kong ranked as the fourth-largest source of foreign investment in the world at US$25 billion, according to a study conducted by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development.
